text:
The failing spec is bandwidth (112 MHz vs. the 140 MHz target). Gain, power, and offset all pass.

M5, the tail current source, is in triode (Vds = 0.225 V, Vdsat = 0.546 V). Its drain sits at the input pair's source node, which is set by the common-mode input (0.9 V) minus the input pair's Vgs (0.674 V). That node cannot rise high enough to keep M5 saturated, so the tail current is limited by triode operation rather than by the mirror. The mirror ratio W5/W6 = 2.02/0.49 ≈ 4.1 predicts about 41 µA, but M5 carries only 26.7 µA. This starves the input pair, so gm1 and the gain-bandwidth product drop. The sensitivities agree: M5 is the strongest bandwidth lever (+12.2% for +20% W), and M6 and M8 follow it through the shared bias chain. Rz has no effect, so the compensation network is not the problem.

M5 is the most likely corrupted element. Its width (or effective mirror ratio) is oversized for the headroom available at the tail node. M6 is second, since it sets the ibias voltage that M5 and M8 mirror. M8 is third, as the output-stage sink whose sensitivity is similar but whose current is consistent with its mirror ratio.

```json
{"ranking": ["M5", "M6", "M8"], "fault": "M5 (tail current source) is oversized relative to its mirror reference M6 (W/L ratio ~4.1 vs. the intended value), so it is pushed into triode (Vds = 0.225 V < Vdsat = 0.546 V) and delivers only ~26.7 uA instead of its mirrored value. This starves the input pair's gm and reduces the closed-loop bandwidth to 112 MHz. Fix by reducing M5 W (or restoring the intended mirror ratio) so the tail stays in saturation with Vds >= Vdsat."}
```
